prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1470; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- Two similar charges on the same day are being checked.
- The repair labor hours fit the damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: The front bumper cover is cracked across the center and the upper radiator support is bent, with the hood latch and both headlamp assemblies broken away from their mounts. Damage is confined to the front end and the pattern is consistent with the reported low-speed frontal contact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and no prior repair records were noted during inspection. Labor hours listed on the estimate fit the scope of the work described. Two similar charges submitted on the same day are currently under review and have not been approved. Repair plan: replace the bumper cover, radiator support, hood latch, and both headlamps, then refinish and recheck alignment before release.
